q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Slow down and keep going if no cars are coming
Come to a complete stop, then go only when it is safe
Stop only if a police officer is present
explain: Texas law requires a full stop at a stop sign unless an officer or a traffic signal tells you to go. After stopping, you yield to traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.

q: You approach an intersection with this sign. What must you do?
options: Slow down, give the right-of-way to cross traffic, and stop if needed
Always come to a full stop before entering
Speed up to merge ahead of cross traffic
explain: At a yield sign you must slow to a reasonable speed and let vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard go first. You stop only when safety requires it.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may enter only to make a U-turn
The road ahead is closed for repairs
Do not drive into this road or ramp; traffic on it comes toward you
explain: This sign is posted where a driver could wrongly enter a one-way road, a divided highway, or a ramp. Entering would put you against the flow of traffic.

q: You see this sign facing you after turning onto a road. What does it tell you?
options: You are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or ramp and must get out of that direction safely
You missed your exit and should back up on the shoulder
The road ahead has a detour
explain: A WRONG WAY sign backs up the DO NOT ENTER sign and is placed farther along a one-way roadway. Seeing it means you are heading against oncoming traffic.

q: What does this sign tell you about the street it points along?
options: Only one lane is open ahead
Vehicles may travel only in the direction of the arrow
You may turn only once on this street
explain: ONE WAY signs mark streets where traffic is allowed to move in one direction only, shown by the arrow.

q: What does this sign prohibit?
options: Left turns
Changing lanes
U-turns
explain: A red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow is a movement prohibition sign: turning around (a U-turn) is not allowed here.

q: What does this sign at an intersection mean?
options: Left turns are not allowed
Left turns are allowed only on a green arrow
The left lane ends ahead
explain: The red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow is a movement prohibition sign that bans left turns from this approach.

q: This sign is posted at a signal where you want to turn right. The light is steady red. What should you do?
options: Stop, then turn right when the way is clear
Stop and wait for a signal that lets you go
Turn right without stopping if no one is in the crosswalk
explain: Texas normally allows a right turn on red after stopping, but a posted sign can prohibit it. With this sign you must wait for a signal that allows the turn.

q: A railroad crossing has only this sign, with no lights, gates, or flagger. What does Texas law require?
options: Always stop, even if no train is near
Nothing special; trains must stop for cars at unmarked crossings
Yield to any train close enough to be a hazard, and stop if safety requires it
explain: At a crossing marked only with crossbucks, you must give trains the right-of-way, go at a reasonable speed, and stop when needed for safety.

q: What does this round yellow sign warn you about?
options: A railroad crossing is ahead
A rest area is ahead
Road repairs are ahead
explain: The round Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign is placed ahead of railroad crossings to give you time to look, listen, and slow down.

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Move into the left lane
Slow down; the road curves to the right ahead
Turn right at the next intersection
explain: This yellow warning sign shows a curve to the right ahead. Texas law requires a reduced, appropriate speed when approaching and going around a curve.

q: What does this sign warn drivers on the main road about?
options: The road ahead is divided by a median
Your lane ends and you must exit
Traffic from another roadway may be merging into your lane ahead
explain: The Merge sign warns that two roadways join ahead, so watch for entering vehicles and adjust your speed or position.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: The number of lanes is reduced ahead, so drivers in the ending lane must merge
A new lane is being added on the right
Passing is allowed on the right
explain: The Lane Ends sign warns that the number of lanes in your direction drops ahead. Drivers in the ending lane must merge into the remaining lane.

q: What does this warning sign tell you?
options: A railroad crossing with lights is ahead
There is a traffic signal ahead that you may not be able to see yet
Traffic signals ahead are not working
explain: The Signal Ahead sign is used before a traffic signal that is hard to see from far away, so you can be ready to stop.

q: What should you expect after passing this sign?
options: A school bus stop
A toll booth
A stop sign ahead, so be ready to stop
explain: The Stop Ahead sign warns of a stop sign that may not be visible in time, giving you room to slow down.

q: You are leaving a divided highway and see this sign. What does it mean?
options: Oncoming traffic will now share the road with you, with no median between
Two lanes of traffic go your direction ahead
You may pass on either side
explain: The Two-Way Traffic sign warns that a divided road is changing to a two-lane road with traffic in both directions.

q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A hiking trail is nearby
People may be crossing the road ahead
Pedestrians are not allowed on this road
explain: The pedestrian warning sign alerts you to a place where people may cross or walk in the road, so slow down and watch for them.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road may become unexpectedly slippery, so slow down when it is wet
Winding road ahead
Do not use your brakes
explain: This sign warns of a surface that can be slippery. Texas law calls for a reduced speed when weather or road conditions create a hazard.

q: This sign is at the front of a median. What does it tell you?
options: Turn right at the median
The right lane is closed
Pass only to the right of the median or obstruction
explain: The Keep Right sign is used where traffic must go only to the right side of a roadway feature such as a median island.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not stop on the roadway
Passing other vehicles is not allowed here
Pedestrians may not pass
explain: The DO NOT PASS sign is a regulatory sign that backs up no-passing pavement markings where passing is unsafe.

q: This pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of a two-lane road. What does it mark?
options: The start of a zone where passing is not allowed
The end of a no-passing zone
A left-turn lane ahead
explain: The NO PASSING ZONE pennant is placed on the left side of the road where a no-passing zone begins.

q: What does this orange sign tell you?
options: A detour is required for all vehicles
The road is closed ahead
You are approaching a work zone, so expect workers, equipment, or lane changes
explain: Orange is the color for temporary traffic control. The ROAD WORK sign is placed in advance of a work area to warn of obstructions or restrictions.

q: What should you be ready to do after this sign?
options: Speed up to get through the work zone quickly
Slow down and follow the directions of a flagger who may stop you
Change lanes to the left
explain: The Flagger sign is placed ahead of a spot where a person is controlling traffic. Be prepared to stop and follow the flagger's signals.

q: What does this blue sign indicate?
options: A hospital that is open 24 hours a day, every day
A hotel nearby
A highway rest area
explain: Blue signs show road-user services. The Hospital sign may only be used for facilities that operate around the clock, seven days a week.

q: This sign is next to the left-turn signal. The light is a steady green ball. What does it mean?
options: You may turn left only on a green arrow
Oncoming traffic must stop for you
You may turn left, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
explain: On a circular green you may turn left, but you must yield to vehicles lawfully in the intersection and to pedestrians. The sign reminds you that the turn is not protected.

q: In Texas, this emblem on the back of a vehicle means the vehicle:
options: Is carrying hazardous materials
Is designed to travel at 25 mph or less
Is about to make a wide turn
explain: Texas requires a slow-moving-vehicle emblem on vehicles built to travel at 25 mph or less, so other drivers can see them early and slow down.

q: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
options: A playground is closed
Children may be playing in a park
You are near a school, where children may be crossing or nearby
explain: The pentagon-shaped School sign warns that you are approaching a school area, a school zone, or a school crossing.

q: Which color is used for signs in road work and other temporary traffic control zones?
explain: Orange is the national color for temporary traffic control, such as work zones.

q: Which color is used for signs that guide you to services such as gas, food, or a hospital?
explain: Blue is reserved for road-user services guidance, tourist information, and evacuation routes.

q: Which color is used on school, pedestrian, and bicycle warning signs?
explain: Fluorescent yellow-green marks warnings about pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, school buses, and schools.

q: Which sign color means stop or that something is prohibited?
explain: Red is used for stop or prohibition, as on STOP, YIELD, and DO NOT ENTER signs.

q: Which sign color points you to parks and other recreational or cultural areas?
explain: Brown signs give guidance to recreational and cultural interest areas.

q: Which color on signs shows direction guidance and movements that are permitted?
explain: Green indicates permitted movements and direction guidance, such as highway guide signs.

q: The round shape is reserved for only one warning sign. Which one?
explain: A circle is used only for the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign, which tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

q: Which of these is a regulatory sign, telling you a rule you must obey?
explain: Regulatory signs give notice of traffic laws; DO NOT PASS is one. The yellow diamonds are warning signs about conditions ahead.

q: You face a steady green light (a full circle, not an arrow). What does Texas law allow?
options: Go straight only; turns need an arrow
Go straight or turn, but yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to pedestrians
Go straight or turn, and pedestrians must wait for you
explain: A circular green lets you go straight or turn unless a sign forbids it. You must still yield to vehicles lawfully in the intersection and stop for pedestrians lawfully crossing.

q: What does a steady yellow traffic light tell you?
options: Speed up to beat the red light
Pedestrians have the right-of-way
The green movement is ending and a red light is coming
explain: A steady yellow warns that the movement allowed by green is ending or that red is about to show, so prepare to stop if you safely can.

q: You are stopped at a steady red light. When may you turn left on red in Texas?
options: From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Never
Whenever there is no oncoming traffic
explain: After a full stop and yielding, Texas allows a left turn on red only when both streets are one-way and the turn is otherwise allowed. A posted sign can forbid it.

q: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: Slow down and go through with caution
Treat it like a stop sign: stop, then go when it is safe
Stop and wait until it turns green
explain: A flashing red means stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or edge of the intersection, then proceed under the same rules as a stop sign.

q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: You may proceed, but only with caution
Come to a full stop
The signal is broken and you must turn around
explain: Facing a flashing yellow, you may go through the intersection or past the signal only with caution.

q: You reach an intersection where the traffic lights are completely dark because of a power outage. What must you do?
options: Go through if the road looks clear, since no signal applies
Yield only to vehicles on your right
Stop as if the intersection had a stop sign
explain: Texas law says a signal showing no light at all is treated like a stop sign (this does not cover freeway ramp meters or pedestrian hybrid beacons).

q: A police officer directing traffic waves you through a red light. What should you do?
options: Wait for the light to turn green
Follow the officer's directions
Honk and wait for the officer to step aside
explain: You must obey traffic-control devices unless a traffic officer, police officer, or escort flagger directs you otherwise.

q: A green arrow is lit for your lane. What does it allow?
options: Moving only in the arrow's direction, while still yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk and traffic lawfully in the intersection
Moving in any direction
Moving in the arrow's direction without watching for anyone
explain: A green arrow lets you enter carefully in the direction shown. You must still yield to pedestrians in an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

q: A red plaque reading ALL-WAY is mounted under a STOP sign. What does it tell you?
options: Cross traffic does not have to stop
Every approach to this intersection has a stop sign
You may turn any direction without stopping
explain: The ALL-WAY plaque is placed under each STOP sign at intersections where traffic on every approach must stop.

q: Unless a sign shows otherwise, the Texas speed limit on a street in an urban district (other than an alley) is ___ mph.
explain: Texas sets a prima facie limit of 30 mph on urban district streets that are not alleys.

q: In an urban district in Texas, the speed limit in an alley is ___ mph unless posted otherwise.
explain: The prima facie limit for an alley in an urban district is 15 mph.

q: Outside an urban district, the Texas speed limit on a US or state-numbered highway is ___ mph unless a different limit is posted.
explain: For passenger vehicles, Texas law sets 70 mph on US and state-numbered highways outside urban districts.

q: Outside an urban district, on a highway that is not numbered by Texas or the United States, the limit is ___ mph unless posted otherwise.
explain: Texas sets 60 mph on highways outside urban districts that do not carry a state or US number.

q: When driving on a Texas beach, the speed limit is ___ mph.
explain: State law sets a 15 mph limit on beaches.

q: On a 60 mph road, you approach a stopped police car with its lights on and cannot move out of the lane next to it. You must slow to at least ___ mph below the posted limit.
explain: If you cannot vacate the lane closest to the vehicle, Texas requires slowing to 20 mph below a posted limit of 25 mph or more.

q: On a section of state highway designed for it and approved after an engineering study, the Texas Transportation Commission may set a speed limit of up to ___ mph.
explain: Texas law lets the commission set a limit of up to 85 mph on highway sections designed for that speed, after an engineering and traffic investigation.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: 65 mph is the recommended speed only
65 mph is the minimum speed
65 mph is the maximum lawful speed under good conditions
explain: A black-on-white Speed Limit sign is a regulatory sign showing the highest speed allowed there. Going faster is evidence your speed is unlawful.

q: You pass this sign during heavy rain with poor visibility. Is driving 65 mph legal?
options: Yes, any speed up to the posted limit is always legal
Not if 65 mph is faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Only if you turn on your hazard lights
explain: Posted limits apply unless a special hazard calls for a slower speed. You may never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions, including weather.

q: You get a speeding ticket after passing this sign, in a work zone posted with a speed limit sign, while workers are present. What happens to the fine?
options: The minimum and maximum fines are doubled
The fine stays the same
The fine is waived if no one was hurt
explain: In a construction or maintenance work zone with workers present, Texas doubles both the minimum and maximum fine. For speeding, the zone must be marked with a sign showing the speed limit.

q: What is the basic speed rule in Texas?
options: Always drive at the posted limit
Never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Keep up with the fastest traffic
explain: Texas law forbids driving faster than is reasonable and prudent given the existing conditions and hazards.

q: Under Texas law, a driver must control speed as needed to:
options: Arrive on time
Save fuel
Avoid hitting any person or vehicle lawfully on or entering the road
explain: Drivers must control their speed to avoid colliding with others who are on or entering the highway lawfully.

q: Texas law requires a reduced speed when you are:
options: Approaching and crossing an intersection or a railroad crossing
Driving on a straight, empty highway
Merging onto a freeway
explain: Approaching and crossing an intersection or railroad grade crossing is one of the situations where the law calls for an appropriate reduced speed.

q: You are approaching the top of a hill and cannot see over it. What does Texas law require?
options: Speed up so you do not lose momentum
Drive at an appropriate reduced speed
Move to the left lane
explain: The law lists approaching a hill crest as a situation that calls for a reduced, appropriate speed, because you cannot see what is ahead.

q: On a narrow, winding road, you should:
options: Drive at the highest speed allowed for the road
Use the center of the road
Reduce your speed
explain: Traveling on a narrow or winding roadway is one of the conditions where Texas law requires a reduced speed.

q: In Texas, driving faster than a prima facie speed limit is:
options: Evidence that your speed is not reasonable and prudent, and is unlawful
Always legal if traffic is light
Only a warning, never a ticket
explain: A speed over the prima facie limit is treated as evidence that the speed is unreasonable and unlawful.

q: Can you get a speeding ticket in Texas while driving below the posted limit?
options: No, the posted limit is always a safe speed
Only at night
Yes, if a special hazard such as fog or ice made that speed unsafe
explain: Posted and statutory limits are lawful only when no special hazard requires a slower speed. You must still drive at a reasonable and prudent speed.

q: For speed limits, Texas defines an "urban district" as an area along a highway where buildings are less than 100 feet apart for a distance of at least:
options: 100 yards
One-quarter mile
One mile
explain: An urban district is territory along a highway with business, industrial, or residential buildings spaced less than 100 feet apart for at least one-quarter mile.

q: How do Texas speed limits differ between day and night?
options: Night limits are always 5 mph lower
They are the same day and night
Night limits apply only on rural highways
explain: Texas requires any entity that sets or changes a speed limit to use the same limit for daytime and nighttime.

q: What speed limit applies to a pickup truck (a light truck) in Texas?
options: The same limit as a passenger car at that time and place
10 mph below the car limit
The truck limit posted for large trucks
explain: Texas law gives light trucks, such as pickups, the same speed limits as passenger cars.

q: Before the Texas Transportation Commission can change a state highway speed limit, what must it rely on?
options: A vote of drivers who use the road
The speed limits of neighboring states
An engineering and traffic investigation
explain: The commission may change a prima facie limit only after an engineering and traffic investigation shows the existing limit is unreasonable or unsafe.

q: When does a new speed limit set by the Texas Transportation Commission take effect?
options: When signs giving notice of the new limit are put up
On January 1 of the next year
As soon as it is published in a newspaper
explain: A limit declared by the commission becomes effective when the commission erects signs showing the new limit.

q: Besides a regular limit, the Texas Transportation Commission may declare a separate speed limit for which condition?
options: Holiday weekends
Wet or inclement weather
Tourist season
explain: The commission may declare a reasonable and safe speed for wet or inclement weather, meaning rain, ice, or snow that makes the road hazardous.

q: A Texas city wants to change the speed limit on one of its streets. What is the highest limit it may set?
options: 65 mph
85 mph
75 mph
explain: A city may change limits by ordinance based on an engineering and traffic investigation, but it may not set a limit above 75 mph.

q: Is it legal in Texas to drive so slowly that you hold up the normal flow of traffic?
options: No, unless the slower speed is needed for safety or to obey the law
Yes, driving slowly is always safe
Yes, as long as you stay in the left lane
explain: Texas prohibits driving so slowly that you impede normal and reasonable traffic, except when reduced speed is needed for safety or required by law.

q: A highway has a posted minimum speed limit. When may you drive slower than it?
options: Whenever you are looking for an exit
Only when necessary for safe operation or to obey the law
Any time you are in the right lane
explain: Where signs give notice of a minimum speed, you may not drive slower except as necessary for safe operation or to comply with the law.

q: Which vehicle is exempt from Texas speed limits?
options: A delivery truck running late
A driver taking a sick friend to the hospital
An ambulance responding to an emergency call
explain: The speed rules do not apply to authorized emergency vehicles responding to a call, police patrols, or a physician or ambulance responding to an emergency call.

q: After a lowered speed limit in a state highway work zone, how will you know the speed limit once the zone ends?
options: A sign at the end of the zone shows the speed limit after the zone
You return to 70 mph automatically
You keep the work zone speed until the next city
explain: An entity that lowers a work zone limit on the state highway system must post a sign at the end of the zone showing the limit that applies afterward.

q: TxDOT posts a temporary lower speed limit at a highway maintenance site. Which limit must you obey there?
options: The usual higher limit, because temporary signs are only advice
The temporary lower limit
Whichever limit other drivers are following
explain: A temporary limit set for a maintenance site is enforceable like any other limit and overrides limits that would allow a higher speed.

q: In Texas, who sets the reduced speed limit in a school crossing zone?
options: The school principal
The State Board of Education
The local authority, such as the city or county
explain: Texas defines a school crossing zone as a reduced-speed zone designated by a local authority to help children cross safely while the reduced limit applies.

q: A sign reads SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT 20 WHEN FLASHING. When does the 20 mph limit apply?
options: While the attached yellow lights are flashing
Only on weekends
All day, every day
explain: The School Speed Limit When Flashing sign marks a reduced school speed zone that is in effect while its beacons flash.

q: You see a yellow REDUCED SPEED LIMIT AHEAD sign. What does it mean?
options: You may ignore the next speed limit sign
The road ahead is closed
A lower speed limit starts at the next Speed Limit sign, so prepare to slow down
explain: This warning sign gives advance notice of a lower limit. It must be followed by a Speed Limit sign showing the same speed where the zone begins.

q: A yellow plaque showing "35 MPH" is mounted under a curve warning sign. What does it tell you?
options: The minimum speed through the curve
The advisory speed recommended for the curve
The speed limit for trucks only
explain: An Advisory Speed plaque supplements a warning sign to show the speed recommended for that condition, based on an engineering study.

q: You are on a farm-to-market road outside an urban district, and no speed limit is posted. What is the limit for a passenger car?
options: 60 mph
55 mph
70 mph
explain: Farm-to-market and ranch-to-market roads count as state-numbered highways, so the 70 mph limit outside urban districts applies.
